Predicates:
GetsMonkeypox(x) ::: x gets Monkeypox.
OccursInVirus(x) ::: x occurs in the Monkeypox virus.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Symptoms(x, y) ::: x has symptoms y.
Fever(x) ::: x has fever.
Headache(x) ::: x has headache.
MusclePain(x) ::: x has muscle pains.
Tiredness(x) ::: x is tired.
FeelsTired(x) ::: x feels tired when x gets the flu.
Flu(x) ::: x has the flu.
HumansAreMammals ::: Humans are mammals.
MammalsAreAnimals ::: Mammals are animals.
MonkeypoxVirusInAnimals ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
Premises:
∀x (OccursInVirus(x) → GetsMonkeypox(x)) ::: When the Monkeypox virus occurs in a being, it may get Monkeypox.
Animal(x) → ∃y (OccursInVirus(y) ∧ x = y) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
HumansAreMammals ::: Humans are mammals.
MammalsAreAnimals ::: Mammals are animals.
Symptoms(x, fever) ∧ Symptoms(x, headache) ∧ Symptoms(x, musclePain) ∧ Symptoms(x, tiredness) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, and tiredness.
FeelsTired(x) → HasFlu(x) ::: People feel tired when they get the flu.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (Flu(x)) ::: No one gets the flu.
